comments.body:
## Cause CONFIRMED — and the prime suspect (2645 / 25d1d683e55a) is REFUTED

**The prime suspect is refuted.** `25d1d683e55a` ("Add probe_source Terraform grounding tool")
did NOT modify the failing test. `git show 25d1d683e55a -- tests/unit/workflow/test_terraform_code_review_tools.py`
is +17/-0 and adds exactly one NEW test (`test_code_review_provider_advertises_probe_source_as_third_tool`)
plus a `_TF_TOOLS_ALL` constant. It does not touch
`test_ac3_verifier_routing_gets_distinct_fresh_terraform_session` at all. Its production diff
(`terraform_tools.py`, `terraform_seam.py`) adds a third tool and drops an unused `_location`
parameter; it changes NOTHING about session lifecycle or routing. The timeline fit was
coincidence.

**The actual cause is the test's own measurement, and the failure is a FLAKE that predates 2645.**
The test recorded `id(session)` for each opened session:

```python
opened.append(id(session))
...
assert len(opened) >= 2 and len(set(opened[:2])) == 2
```

The IaC pass's session is dropped before the verify pass opens its own — nothing retains it,
because only the integer `id()` was kept. CPython recycles the address of a freed object, so two
genuinely distinct sessions can report the same `id()`. `1 == 2` is an allocator artifact, not a
routing defect.

### Reproduction, with the extra installed (AC1)

`python-hcl2==8.1.3` (the `grounding-terraform` extra) installed into the worktree venv; test
confirmed EXECUTING, not skipping (6-10 s runtime, versus the 3.86 s skip in the ticket).

- 8 runs: 1 failure. 12 further runs: 1 failure. Roughly 12%.
- The captured failure is byte-identical to CI: `E assert (2 >= 2 and 1 == 2)` at the
  `len(set(opened[:2])) == 2` line.

### Proof the routing is CORRECT and only the measurement was wrong (AC2)

A probe variant that holds a STRONG reference to each session (so no address can be recycled) and
compares by identity ran 10/10 green, printing distinct addresses every time:

```
PROBE distinct-objs: True ids: [4499179184, 4486049584]
PROBE distinct-objs: True ids: [4530306944, 4530785072]
... (10/10)
```

Separately, plain CPython demonstrates the recycling directly: three sequentially-allocated and
freed objects returned `distinct: 1` — one id for three objects.

So the production contract holds: `_open_session_tools` calls `tft.open_session` once per routed
call, and the IaC and verify passes always receive two distinct fresh sessions.

### Which side is fixed, and why (AC4)

**The test is fixed, not the code — and the assertion is STRENGTHENED, not relaxed.** The old
contract ("verifier routing gets a distinct fresh terraform session") is unchanged and still fully
enforced; only the way it is measured changes. `id()` on objects whose lifetimes do not overlap is
not a valid identity token, so the old check was an unsound proxy that could report a false
failure (and, symmetrically, could have hidden a real one). Holding the session objects and
asserting `opened[0] is not opened[1]` tests the same contract soundly.

### Seeded-defect evidence (the fixed test still catches a REAL regression)

A genuine session-reuse defect was seeded into `_open_session_tools` (module-level cache so both
passes share one session). The fixed test FAILED 3/3 — deterministically, where the old
`id()`-based test would have been unreliable. The seam was then restored and
`git diff -- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/terraform_seam.py` is empty.

### Verification

- Fixed test: 0 failures in 25 runs (baseline ~12%).
- Whole file `tests/unit/workflow/test_terraform_code_review_tools.py`: 13 passed.
- `make lint` exit 0; complexity ratchet `new=0 increased=0`; mechanism ratchet
  `new=0 increased=0`; `make typecheck` clean (764 files).

### Sweep lanes (AC5)

`macos full suite`, `py3.15`, `py3.14t` are **DIFFERENT-cause** — all three fail identically on
`tests/interfaces/store/test_reconciler_apply_bindings.py::test_reconcile_once_threads_composed_runtime_transport_into_apply`
(`assert None is namespace(name='composed-transport')`), a different subsystem and a deterministic
failure rather than this ~12% flake. Filed separately as `ae96-72a9-8145-4c85`
(`primordial-ardent-zethuswasp`), linked `discovered_from` this ticket. `sweep (windows)` is
`continue-on-error` and left to the Windows epic.

## Main is RED on the gating cell

Scheduled Test Suite run `33950878570` (2026-09-05 06:49 UTC, `headSha a33333b8709a`) failed the
**gating** cell `build-and-test / pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.13)`:

```
FAILED tests/unit/workflow/test_terraform_code_review_tools.py::
       test_ac3_verifier_routing_gets_distinct_fresh_terraform_session
    assert len(opened) >= 2 and len(set(opened[:2])) == 2
E   assert (2 >= 2 and 1 == 2)
```

Two sessions were opened, but they were the SAME session — `set(opened[:2])` has one element where
the test requires two distinct ones. The test's name states the contract: the verifier routing must
get a *distinct fresh* terraform session.

Four `sweep` lanes also failed in the same run (`macos full suite`, `py3.15`, `py3.14t`,
`windows`). `sweep (windows)` is `continue-on-error` by design and is tracked by the Windows
support-target epic; the other three sweep lanes are NOT yet triaged and may or may not share this
cause — establish that rather than assuming it.

## Prime suspect, stated as a LEAD not a finding

`git log` shows the failing test file was last modified by **`25d1d683e55a` — "Add probe_source
Terraform grounding tool"** (Gerrit change 2645), which also added the `probe_source` tool to
`src/rebar/grounding/`. That change modified both the test and the module under test.

Timeline supports it but does not prove it:

    01:07 UTC   scheduled Test Suite  SUCCESS
    ~05:xx      25d1d683e55a merges
    06:49 UTC   scheduled Test Suite  FAILURE, in a test that commit touched

A session-routing change that makes two calls share one session is exactly the shape of `1 == 2`
here. But confirm by bisecting or by reading the diff — do not assume.

## It does NOT reproduce on a default local checkout

```
$ pytest tests/unit/workflow/test_terraform_code_review_tools.py::test_ac3_... -q
1 skipped in 3.86s
```

The test opens with `pytest.importorskip("hcl2")`, so it SKIPS wherever the `hcl2` extra is absent.
CI runs it because that lane sets `REBAR_REQUIRE_EXTRAS=1`, which turns an `importorskip` that
would skip into a hard error. **Install the extra before attempting a reproduction**, or the test
will silently not run and a green local result will mean nothing — the same skip-is-not-a-pass
trap this repo has already been bitten by (bug `599e`, and the chromium tier in `337e`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The failure is REPRODUCED locally with the `hcl2` extra installed, and the reproduction is
      shown failing for the stated reason (`1 == 2` on distinct sessions) rather than erroring or
      skipping.
- [ ] The cause is established by evidence — diff reading or bisect — and named. If `25d1d683e55a`
      is NOT the cause, say so and name what is; a refuted lead is a valid outcome.
- [ ] The gating cell `build-and-test / pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.13)` passes on `main`.
- [ ] Whichever side was wrong is fixed on its merits: either the routing genuinely lost session
      distinctness (fix the code) or the test's expectation is stale against a deliberate design
      change (fix the test AND state why the old contract no longer holds). Do not simply relax the
      assertion to make it pass.
- [ ] The three untriaged sweep-lane failures (`macos full suite`, `py3.15`, `py3.14t`) are each
      recorded as same-cause or different-cause with evidence. Do not fold them in silently.
